main_text.l: Vel adstringentes: ut Granatorum, Juglandium viridium, &c.
Radicum cortices vel calidi sunt in secundo, ut Capparis, vel frigidi in tertio gradu, ut Mandragorae, &c.
Purgantes vero vel purgant Bilem & Pituitam, vel Aquam.
Bilem & Pituitam: cortex Esulae, Cucumeris sylvestris. Aquam; Sambuci, Ebuli, &c.
Succus proprie dicitur, qui contusione & conquassatione exprimitur, vel ex Herbis, Fructibus, aut Seminibus, &c.
Herbarum succi vel manifeste alterant vel occulte.
Succi primo gradu calidi sunt, Absinthii, Brassicæ, &c.
Secundo; Apii, Calaminthae, Lupuli, Mentae, Rutae, Scordii, &c.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the left are set in italic type and placed beside the paragraphs they stand against. The word "Braffica" is printed with a long s, read as Brassicæ. Italic type is judged from the scan and some words are uncertain. The catchword "Quar-" is printed at the lower right corner.
